machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.5 (bundled, static: linux-ext-libs 1.26); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: Written on 2026-10-25, before the tag. 7.28.5 is the C code of main at f5a86a1b2, measured against 7.28.4, the last release with a study. A short study: 7.28.5 writes again code of others the SDK could not carry under its license, and only two of those changes are on the path of a benchmark: the string switch (SWITCHS) of helpers.h, which tr_treedb runs, and the websocket handshake (SHA-1 and base64), which perf_ievent runs once per connection. So only the benchmarks of the treedb (perf_tr_treedb, perf_tr_treedb_read, perf_c_treedb) and of the inter-yuno events (perf_ievent) were run; the other figures pass through no changed code and are not in this study (their last measure is the study of 7.28.4). Each release built from a git worktree with the same .config, compiler and outputs_ext (linux-ext-libs 1.26); the kernel libraries, the modules and the four benchmarks were built in each. The two binaries of each benchmark run in rotation, the order turned every round, with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run: 8 rounds. Mean +- standard deviation (median), t = the change over its standard error; |t| < 3 is noise. The treedb figures are CPU time of the process per operation.
method.tag_run: The absolute figures of 7.28.5 are its side of the A/B run: its C code (f5a86a1b2), built on 2026-10-25 on the machine of the earlier reports. The binary sizes are those of the yunos built from the main tree with the same .config.

story.title: Yuneta 7.28.5: its own code, at the same speed
story.lead: 7.28.5 writes again the code of others that the MIT license of the SDK cannot carry. Against 7.28.4, the 18 figures that run changed code stay inside their noise.
tiles: treedb: update a node and save it
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built from the tree of each release (7.28.4 and 7.28.5), the binaries run in rotation: 8 rounds. Only the benchmarks that run changed code. A change inside its whisker is noise.
story.prices_sub: What got slower, how much, in which release, and what it buys.
story.abs_sub: Absolute figures of the 7.28.5 build (its C code: f5a86a1b2), measured on 2026-10-25 as its side of the A/B run.
